b2-chileextremos-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Sky of Atacama
b2-chileextremos-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Atacama Desert, and he asks why astronomers work there.
b2-chileextremos-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what makes Atacama special for astronomy.
cues: Say what makes the desert special for astronomers
Stress it with a cleft sentence
b2-chileextremos-01.target: Lo que hace especial a Atacama es su cielo despejado.
b2-chileextremos-01.english: What makes Atacama special is its clear sky.
b2-chileextremos-01.canDo: I can put one fact about Atacama in the spotlight with a cleft sentence (*lo que… es…*, *fue… cuando…*, *fue… donde…*).

b2-chileextremos-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How Copper Is Obtained
b2-chileextremos-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about copper mining in northern Chile, and she asks how the copper is obtained.
b2-chileextremos-02.prompt: Tell Meg one step of how copper is obtained.
cues: Say what is done with the rock first
Do not say who does it
b2-chileextremos-02.target: Primero se rompe la roca y después se aplica la lixiviación.
b2-chileextremos-02.english: First the rock is broken, and then leaching is applied.
b2-chileextremos-02.canDo: I can describe how copper is obtained with the passive *se* (*se tritura la roca*, *se construyen plantas*).

b2-chileextremos-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Says What
b2-chileextremos-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Mapuche, and he asks you what the organisations in the film want.
b2-chileextremos-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the Mapuche organisations say about the land.
b2-chileextremos-03.target: Las organizaciones mapuche dicen que el Estado debe devolver las tierras.
b2-chileextremos-03.english: Mapuche organisations say that the state must return the land.
b2-chileextremos-03.canDo: I can report who says what with *según* and *dice que* when a subject is disputed.

b2-chileextremos-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Again in Patagonia
b2-chileextremos-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to southern Chile, and she asks if people visit Torres del Paine more than once.
b2-chileextremos-04.prompt: Tell Meg that many travellers go to the park again.
cues: Say that many travellers do it
Say that they visit the park a second time
b2-chileextremos-04.target: Muchos viajeros vuelven a visitar Torres del Paine.
b2-chileextremos-04.english: Many travellers visit Torres del Paine again.
b2-chileextremos-04.canDo: I can say that something happens again with *volver a* + infinitive (*el viento vuelve a soplar*, *no volverán a crecer*).

b2-chileextremos-05.title: Communicative Challenge: If There Were More Lines
b2-chileextremos-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about solar energy in Chile, and he asks what the problem is.
b2-chileextremos-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what would happen with more transmission lines.
b2-chileextremos-05.target: Si hubiera más líneas de transmisión, se aprovecharía mejor la energía solar.
b2-chileextremos-05.english: If there were more transmission lines, solar energy would be used better.
b2-chileextremos-05.canDo: I can imagine a different situation with *si* + imperfect subjunctive + conditional (*si hubiera más líneas, se aprovecharía más energía*).

b2-chileextremos-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: From Atacama to Patagonia
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a whole documentary about Chile, and she asks what surprised you most.
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact you learned, using a cleft sentence.
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.target: Fue en el llano de Chajnantor donde se instaló ALMA.
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.english: It was on the Chajnantor plateau that ALMA was built.
b2-chileextremos-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the extreme landscapes of Chile, from Atacama to Patagonia.
